title: Trial OR-Tools (SCIP / CP-SAT) as the quantization integer program backend against the model suite and the T-Rex skull
user-messages: have agent run its recommendation against the suite of models and skull, i think we used to use or tools for something
description:
Trial Google OR-Tools (com.google.ortools:ortools-java, Apache-2.0) as a backend for the quantization integer program (quantization/IntegerProgram.java, called from QuantizedMeshGrid), against the existing hand-written dense-tableau branch-and-bound, on the model suite and the T-Rex skull.

Why: on the full-resolution Trellis T-Rex skull (700k faces) the quantization program is 5,375 variables, presolved to 2,828 columns × 2,727 rows, mostly one connected piece. The existing branch-and-bound ran out of an 8 GB heap on it. CRAW-114 changes it to keep open nodes as bounds only and to plunge for an early incumbent, but proving optimality may still take very long. A research pass (2026-11-21) recommended OR-Tools 9.15 with its bundled SCIP 10, single-threaded, with CP-SAT benchmarked alongside and HiGHS as runner-up.

Design, as researched:
- An IntegerProgram backend seam. OR-Tools is used when its natives load; otherwise the existing solver runs, found the way PardisoBackend detects MKL (catch LinkageError/RuntimeException, log the fallback).
- IntegerProgram's own presolve and cover domination stay, and the reduced program is handed to the backend.
- The existing tie-break (most zeros, then lexicographically smallest) stays the canonical answer, expressed as three lexicographic solves: optimum f*; fix w·x <= f*(1+1e-9) and minimise the non-zero indicators; fix that count and minimise each variable in index order.
- Natives per platform in the existing windows/linux/macos-aarch64 pom profiles, following the MKL pattern, and never on the web-teavm build's path.

This is a trial: measure first, and keep the dependency only if the numbers justify it.
definition-of-done:
1. Every model in `ixdar-cli list-meshes` that the pipeline handles today (bolt buddha fandisk feline hand sphere_base block botijo elk fertility rockerarm; sphere_random is excluded per CLAUDE.md), plus the T-Rex skull, is run through quantization with the existing solver and with OR-Tools (SCIP, and CP-SAT where it applies). For each, record quantize wall time, objective, zero-arc count, whether values[] are identical, and the final quad, patch and cone counts.
2. On every model where the existing solver finishes, the OR-Tools backend gives identical values[] in every separation round (objective within 1e-9), so the final layouts are identical. Fertility stays at 11582 quads, 254 patches, 40 cones.
3. The skull's quantization finishes under OR-Tools, with time and gap recorded. Also record whether the existing solver (with CRAW-114's bounds-only frontier, if available) finishes, and how long it takes.
4. Results are in tmp/craw-116-measurements.json and summarised on the ticket, with a recommendation: adopt, adopt behind a flag, or drop.
5. If adopted: the web-teavm build still builds without OR-Tools on its path; build checkstyle-green; the quad layout tests pass.
testing-plan:
1. Unit test: one small IntegerProgram with tied optima, solved by both backends, giving identical values (the tie-break).
2. A debug flag that solves each quantization program with both backends and asserts identical values in every round; run it over the model suite.
3. Skull: run once with each backend. Its seamless stage alone takes about 7.5 minutes until CRAW-115 lands, so budget for it.
4. `mvn -q compile` for the web-teavm profile, to show OR-Tools is not on its path.
unknowns: Whether OR-Tools' Maven natives include HiGHS (MPSolver.createSolver("HIGHS") returns null if not).
Size of the OR-Tools native jars, and whether protobuf-java conflicts with anything on the classpath.
The user recalls OR-Tools being used for something before; no trace found in any repo under C:/Code.
changes-made: Trial results (tmp/craw-116-measurements.json). Suite, cross-check mode (branch and bound, SCIP 1 thread, CP-SAT 8 workers): values identical in every round on bolt buddha feline hand sphere_base block botijo elk fertility rockerarm; objectives equal; fertility 11582 quads / 254 patches / 40 cones under every engine. Fandisk: 2 variables differ (x90/x91, equal weight): OR-Tools returns the lexicographically smaller vector, so branch and bound's tie detection misses this tie; extraction then fails for every backend (PATCH-126, pre-existing). Solve time after presolve, B&B vs SCIP vs CP-SAT: feline 0.07/3.4/13.3 s, botijo 0.009/0.83/3.8 s, fertility 0.004/0.28/2.3 s; branch and bound is 10-100x faster on every suite model. Skull, every engine capped at 900 s: old program (5375 vars, 2828x2727): SCIP proves the minimum weight 5829174.242 in 1.2 s and CP-SAT in 15.6 s, but neither finishes the tie-break (SCIP: per-variable lexicographic stage at x32; CP-SAT: most-zeros stage 2973 vs bound 2918); branch and bound hits the cap, no OOM in 4 GB. Clean map (craw-115 files copied in, 0 flips, still 57179 patches, 5259 vars, 2781x2508): SCIP weight optimum 37756.010 in 0.22 s, most zeros 2953 optimal at 45.7 s, then the lexicographic stage (one MIP per variable, ~2.3 s each) was at x977 of 5259 after 374 solves when the cap hit; CP-SAT most zeros at 275.7 s then capped; branch and bound capped. Recommendation: drop as designed. OR-Tools only wins on the skull's first two stages, and the canonical tie-break as specified (one MIP per variable) does not finish there either, while branch and bound is far faster on every model that finishes.

Re-measured after CRAW-118 removed the tie-break (synced onto master f9e3ad24; every engine solves the weight objective only and keeps its first optimum; tmp/craw-116-measurements.json). Suite (bolt buddha feline hand sphere_base block botijo elk fertility rockerarm fandisk), cross-check run plus one run per engine: SCIP and CP-SAT values identical to branch and bound on every model, objectives equal, final quads/patches/cones identical under all three engines; fertility 11582/254/40; fandisk now extracts (16960/265/30). Solve seconds B&B / SCIP / CP-SAT: feline 0.093/0.024/1.79, elk 0.066/0.024/1.42, botijo 0.007/0.079/1.40, fertility 0.003/0.016/1.57, the rest under 0.005 / 0.017 / 1.9. T-Rex skull end to end (repair_mesh with unfold, 5285 vars, 2788x2527 after presolve, one round): SCIP OPTIMAL 37605.195 in 0.18 s, CP-SAT the identical vector in 7.9 s; branch and bound OutOfMemoryError within seconds (default heap end to end, and 4 GB on the dumped program). With either OR-Tools engine the skull reaches 57277 patches / 1021 cones and then fails in patch grid mapping: patch 8553 boundary is pinched (PatchRegionMapper), downstream of quantization. Recommendation: keep SCIP as the quantization backend, branch and bound as fallback when the natives do not load.

Skull past quantization (SCIP): the PatchRegionMapper pinch on patch 8553 is not made by contraction, recarve or the zero-arc collapse. The patch is already a slit at T-mesh assembly (patch 45996): its side 1 and side 2 are the same arc 83415, flanked by the patch on both sides, ending at critical node 703 = vertex 200672 with index4 = +3, a valence-1 cone whose one trace has the same patch on both sides. KCP13 itself sees only one -1 triangle around that vertex (incident triangle indices -1,0,0,0); the +3 comes from converting the field to vertex cones. Cause: the repaired skull mesh is not 4-smooth in the sense of KCP13 Appendix B (|n*kappa_t| < pi per triangle, kappa_t = sum s_i theta_i - pi, s_i = 2pi/vertex angle sum). 12 triangles break it (nKappa up to 6.47), and they are exactly the neighbourhoods of every high-index or phantom cone (vertices 2051, 167254, 167267, 167473, 200672, 200695, 263959, 270488, 276428). Raw triangle index sum -193 against 4chi = -184 shows the discrete Poincare-Hopf failing there. Cone histogram index4 -3:1, -2:10, +2:5, +3:1. KCP13 covers only n-smooth meshes, so this is a case outside the papers: no fix applied. The options (refine or repair those triangles until the mesh is n-smooth, or support valence-1 cones in patch mapping) are the user's call. The seamless alignment guard (dropCollapsingAlignments) did not fire on the skull (alignment rows 0).

KCP13 n-smooth precondition (user chose option 1). A new stage, refine_n_smooth (RefineNSmoothNode over quadlayout/NSmoothRefinement), runs inside the quad_layout group between split_feature_corners and the cross field, and its output also feeds the motorcycle graph. It splits, for each triangle with |4 kappa_t| >= pi (KCP13 Appendix B), the edge opposite its worst corner term (s_v - 1) theta_v at the midpoint. That leaves every angle sum unchanged and makes the new vertex flat. It repeats until no triangle breaks the condition, carries the alignment slot through the splits, throws after 64 rounds, and returns the input bundle itself when nothing breaks it. Permanent checks in NDirectionField, both citing KCP13 Appendix B: build() refuses a mesh that is not n-smooth (TriangleCurvature.requireNSmooth names the first 8 triangles); after the cones are found, a closed mesh must have triangle-index sum = cone sum = 4chi. Skull: 15 triangles broke the condition before refinement (18 edge splits, 2 rounds), 0 after; triangle sum -184 = 4chi (was -193); no +3 cone remains (index4 histogram: -4:1, -2:6, -1:593, +1:415, +2:5); 0 pinched patches. The skull now gets past patch mapping, then hits OutOfMemoryError in GridMapOptimizer.build during the Newton relax at the default heap. The unrefined skull through cross_field alone throws the n-smooth refusal. Suite: refine_n_smooth changed no suite mesh; quads, patches, cones, objective and zero arcs match the SCIP rows of tmp/craw-116-measurements.json; fertility 11582/254/40. New unit test NSmoothRefinementTest: a cube is refused, refined until its cones sum to 8, and a flat grid comes back as the same instance. The diagnostics are removed.

Archived 2026-11-22 without landing, as tag archive/craw-116 at cff1055e: OR-Tools trial: identical values on 10 of 11 suite models but branch and bound is 10-100x faster on every one; on the skull SCIP and CP-SAT prove the weight optimum fast but neither finishes the tie-break in 900 s. Recommendation was drop; CRAW-119 and CRAW-124 since made the existing solver handle the skull in 2.9 s.
review-summary: IntegerProgram hands the quantization program to OR-Tools SCIP when its natives load, keeping the hand-written branch and bound as the fallback. Branch and bound runs out of memory on scan-sized meshes such as the T-Rex skull, which SCIP solves to the same optimum within a second.
